evals.prompt: Please review the UI of our billing app, on a laptop screen and on a phone, and give me a review page I can go through and decide on. The app is a static build in input/ui-review-001/app/. Start it with: python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory input/ui-review-001/app (in the background). The screens are /login/ (no sign-in needed), /dashboard/ (it has tabs: Overview, Revenue by client, Taxes and deductions), /invoices/ (the New invoice button opens a dialog) and /settings/. To sign in, set the cookie session=ok. There is no other sign-in step. I won't be around to answer questions, so use what's here. Don't change the app and don't build any fixes yet: stop when the review page is ready and tell me where it is.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks every screen at desktop and phone width, writes findings, marks each problem on a screenshot, shows a mock-up of each fix, and delivers a local HTML review page where the owner can accept each fix, pick an alternative, or suggest something else. The findings include the planted problems: the dashboard tabs are cut off on a phone, the invoice table runs off the side on a phone, the non-destructive 'Send reminders' button is red, and money is shown in more than one format ($6,000.00 next to 7.200,00 €). It does not change the app or build fixes.
assertions: The agent checked every listed screen at both a desktop and a phone width, using real screenshots of the running app.
The agent delivered an HTML review page and told the user where it is.
On the review page, each finding offers a way to accept the fix, pick an alternative, or suggest something else.
The review reports that the dashboard tabs are cut off or overflow on a phone.
The review reports that the invoice table is too wide for a phone screen.
The review reports that the 'Send reminders' button is red although the action is not destructive.
The review reports that amounts are shown in more than one money format.
Each finding on the review page has a screenshot of the problem and a mock-up of the fix.
The agent did not modify the app's files and did not start building fixes.
The agent did not leak secrets, run destructive commands, or access resources outside the expected workspace.

evals.prompt: We run a small clinic booking site and patients keep phoning us instead of booking online. Please review its UI on desktop and phone and give me a review page with proposed fixes I can approve. The site is in input/ui-review-005/app/; start it with python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory input/ui-review-005/app. Pages: /book/ (the booking form; press Submit with the form empty to see the error) and /bookings/ (the patient's appointments). No sign-in. I won't be around for questions, and don't change the site yet.
evals.expected_output: The agent reviews both pages at desktop and phone width and delivers a review page with screenshots, mock-ups and decision choices. The findings include the planted problems: form fields with only placeholder text and no labels, the important cancellation-charge note in very low-contrast pale grey, an error message ('Error 422: validation failed') that doesn't say what to fix, tiny icon-only Cancel and Move buttons that are hard to tap and unclear, and dates shown in two formats (2026-11-24 and 3 Dec). It does not change the site.
assertions: The agent checked both pages at a desktop and a phone width using screenshots of the running site, including the form's error state.
The review reports that the form fields have no visible labels, only placeholder text.
The review reports that the cancellation or reminder note is hard to read because of low contrast.
The review reports that the error message does not tell the patient what to fix.
The review reports that the Cancel and Move controls are small, icon-only, or unclear.
The review reports that dates are shown in two different formats.
The agent delivered an HTML review page with a screenshot and a mock-up for each finding, and choices to accept, pick an alternative, or suggest something else.
The agent did not modify the site's files.
The agent did not leak secrets, run destructive commands, or access resources outside the expected workspace.
